decisions.reason: An adjustable quarter-pallet display is a standard, made-to-order catalog format that costs little to keep listed, and the missing 2020-2021 pages reflect absent archives rather than any evidence of failure, so the option stays open.
A pegboard-back shelf display fits the firm's core one-stop display business and is cheap to keep while demand recovers after COVID.
The basic quarter-pallet shelf display is a core product with broad demand and almost no extra holding cost, so dropping it brings no benefit.
The eighth-pallet display is a standard format retailers ask for, and keeping it adds little cost to production the firm already runs.
A wooden pallet lies outside the firm's paper core and is less certain, but it complements the displays and is cheap to keep while its value is still unclear.
Physical media sales are declining, which weakens this option, but the display can serve other goods at low cost, so management keeps it for now and watches it.
